questions.title: Sign-In Strength
questions.question: Think of everyone who can log in to your Notion. How do they sign in?

A.text: Everyone has 2-step verification turned on, in Notion or in the company Google or Microsoft login they use for Notion.

B.text: I have 2-step verification on, but I'm not sure about everyone else.

C.text: Most of us sign in with a password or an email code only.

questions.risk: one phished password opens every page that person can see. Notion can't force 2-step verification on members on any plan, so it comes down to each person.

fixes.text: Each person: Settings → your name → Account security → 2-step verification → Add verification method. Use an authenticator app and save the backup codes.
Make it a written team rule and check it person by person once a quarter.
If the team signs in with Google or Microsoft, turn on 2-step verification in that account too (general guidance, outside Notion).

plan_notes.text: All plans: 2-step verification. It needs a password on the account.
Business and Enterprise: SAML SSO. Settings → Identity → verify domain → Enable SAML SSO → Login method "Only SAML SSO". Remove all Allowed email domains first.
Enterprise only: organization owners can require MFA for guests. Free, Plus and Business alternative: ask guests to turn on 2-step verification before you share client pages.

questions.title: One Person, One Account, Right Access Type
questions.question: Does everyone who opens your workspace use their own account, with the right type of access (staff as members, clients and freelancers as guests on specific pages)?

A.text: Yes. Everyone has their own account, staff are members, and outsiders are guests on only the pages they need.

B.text: Own accounts, but some freelancers or clients are full members.

questions.risk: a shared login means no one is accountable and you can't remove one person without locking out others. An outsider added as a member can open every open teamspace.

fixes.text: Give every person their own account. Retire shared logins.
Settings → People (or Members) → Members tab. Remove outsiders, then re-invite them as guests on specific pages (Share → invite → Skip for now).
Settings → General → Allowed email domains: list only your company domain. Anyone with a listed domain can join as a member.

plan_notes.text: Guest limit: Free 10; Plus, Business and Enterprise unlimited.
Restricted members (for people who need a whole teamspace but not the rest of the workspace) are described in the help center without a plan.

questions.title: Public Pages and Links
questions.question: Are any of your Notion pages open to the public, as a published site or with "Anyone on the web with link"?

A.text: Only pages we meant to make public, and we checked the full list in the last 3 months.

B.text: Only pages we meant to make public, but we haven't checked in a while.

C.text: Probably some old ones nobody has checked.

questions.risk: anyone with the link (or a search engine, if indexing is on) can read the page and all its subpages, and the page data includes contributors' names and emails.

fixes.text: Share → Publish → All published sites: review the list and Unpublish anything that shouldn't be live. Subpages are published too.
Share → General access: if a page says "Anyone on the web with link" and shouldn't, select Remove. Unpublishing a site doesn't turn this off.
For links that must stay open (for example a client proposal): set Link expires in the same dropdown.

plan_notes.text: Enterprise only: Settings → Security → Disable publishing sites, forms, and public links. Free, Plus and Business alternative: the quarterly review above, owned by one named person.

questions.title: Sensitive Data in Pages
questions.question: Do any pages hold passwords, API keys, bank or card details, ID scans, or client personal data?

A.text: No. Passwords and keys live in a password manager, and client personal data sits only on restricted pages.

B.text: A few logins or client details, on pages only the right people can open.

C.text: Yes, on pages the whole team, guests or connected tools can open.

questions.risk: everyone with access, every connected tool and every public link can read them. Deleting the text later is not enough: old versions stay in version history, and deleted pages stay in Trash for 30 days by default.

fixes.text: Search the workspace for "password", "login", "IBAN", "API key" and "passport". List every page that comes up.
Move secrets to a password manager, delete them from the page, then change every password or key that was ever stored in Notion.
Restrict pages that must keep personal data: Share → remove everyone who doesn't need it.

plan_notes.text: Enterprise only: Security and Compliance connections (DLP) can detect sensitive content. Free, Plus and Business alternative: the search above, repeated each quarter.

questions.title: Connected Apps
questions.question: Think of the apps connected to your Notion (Zapier, Make, Slack, form or calendar tools). Which is closest?

A.text: We know every connection, each one has an owner, and we removed unused ones in the last 3 months.

B.text: A few connections, probably all still used, never reviewed.

C.text: Many, added by different people over time.

questions.risk: each connection is a vendor holding a key to the pages it was given. Forgotten connections and copied tokens keep working after the project, and after the person who set them up leaves.

fixes.text: Settings → Connections → Manage: review each one, and select ••• → Disconnect for anything unused or unknown.
On sensitive pages: ••• → More → Connections. Disconnect what doesn't need that page.
If an internal connection token was ever shared: Settings → Connections → Develop or manage connections → find the connection → Refresh, then update every tool that used it.

plan_notes.text: Enterprise only: restrict which connections members can install and keep an approved list. Free, Plus and Business alternative: a one-page list of approved connections with an owner each, checked quarterly.

questions.title: AI Tools
questions.question: Have AI tools been connected to your Notion (for example ChatGPT, Claude or AI agents)?

A.text: None, or only tools we approved, limited to the pages they need.

B.text: Yes, I connected one, and it can reach most of the workspace.

C.text: Yes, people connect their own AI tools and nobody tracks it.

questions.risk: an AI tool reads everything it can reach. Broad access puts client and finance pages in scope, and text inside a page can try to steer an AI tool that reads it (prompt injection).

fixes.text: Settings → Connections: find each AI tool, check who installed it, and disconnect what isn't approved.
Give AI tools access to specific pages, never the whole workspace, and keep finance, HR and client pages out of scope.
Write a short team rule: which AI tools are approved, and who approves new ones.

plan_notes.text: Enterprise only: approved connections list, and the audit log records when external AI tools connect or read pages. Free, Plus and Business alternative: the team rule and quarterly review above.

questions.title: Leavers
questions.question: When someone leaves (staff or contractor), what happens to their Notion access?

A.text: Removed on their last day with a checklist, and their pages are handed over first.

B.text: Removed, but not always right away.

questions.risk: ex-staff and ex-contractors can still open, copy or delete company pages, and the tools they connected keep running.

fixes.text: Before removal: move their work pages out of their Private section into a teamspace. A removed member's private pages are hidden.
Settings → People (or Members) → Members or Guests tab → Remove from workspace. Access ends instantly.
Disconnect connections they set up, and change shared passwords they knew.
Keep a one-page leaver checklist in your ops teamspace and run it on the last day.

plan_notes.text: Enterprise only: user provisioning (SCIM) removes people automatically when they leave your identity provider. Free, Plus and Business alternative: the leaver checklist.

questions.solo_na: Not applicable: only I have ever had access

questions.title: Access Review
questions.question: When did someone last go through the full list of members and guests and remove who no longer needs access?

A.text: In the last 3 months, and it's on a schedule.

questions.risk: access only ever grows. Old clients, past freelancers and people who changed roles keep access no one remembers giving.

fixes.text: Settings → People (or Members): go through the Members and Guests tabs and remove anyone who no longer needs access.
Put a quarterly 20-minute access review on the owner's calendar.
Use permission groups by role (for example "Sales", "Ops") so access follows the role, not the person.

plan_notes.text: Business and Enterprise: Settings → General → Export members as CSV, to review the list offline.

questions.solo_na: Not applicable: only I have ever had access

questions.title: Admin Rights
questions.question: How many people are Workspace owners (full admin rights) in your Notion?

C.text: 3 or more, or I'm not sure who.

questions.risk: every workspace owner can change all security settings, remove people, export everything or delete the workspace. Too many owners means too many master keys; one owner means a lockout if that account is lost.

fixes.text: Settings → People (or Members) → Members tab: change anyone who doesn't need full admin rights from Workspace owner to Member. Keep 2 named owners.
Both owners turn on 2-step verification (Q1).

plan_notes.text: Enterprise only: membership admins and granular admin roles, for people who manage members without full admin rights. Free, Plus and Business alternative: keep 2 owners and let them handle member changes.

questions.title: Default Access
questions.question: When someone new joins your workspace, what can they open on day one?

A.text: Only the areas for their role. Finance, HR and client areas are closed off.

B.text: Everything, but sensitive pages are view-only or locked.

C.text: Everything, and they can edit or share it.

questions.risk: every new hire, freelancer turned member or compromised account can read, change or reshare finance, HR and client pages on day one.

fixes.text: Sidebar → hover a teamspace → ••• → Teamspace settings → Permissions: set sensitive teamspaces to Closed and give everyone else the lowest access that works.
Same window → Members tab: turn off Make default teamspace for sensitive teamspaces.
Key pages: ••• → toggle on Lock page, so they can't be changed by accident.
Settings → Teamspaces → toggle on Limit teamspace creation to only workspace owners.
fixes.verify: plan: the help center doesn't name one

plan_notes.text: Business and Enterprise: Private teamspaces (hidden from people not added), advanced teamspace permissions and granular database permissions. Free and Plus alternative: Closed teamspaces plus page-level sharing.
Enterprise only: per-teamspace Disable guests and Disable export.

questions.title: Recovery Readiness
questions.control: recovery readiness and single points of failure
questions.question: If a key page were deleted tomorrow, or the person who runs it left, how ready are you to get it back?

A.text: Ready. We know how long Trash and version history keep things on our plan, at least 2 people can restore our key pages, and none of them sit in one person's private pages.

B.text: We know Trash and version history exist, but not how long they keep things or who can restore.

C.text: We'd have to rebuild from memory or ask Notion support.

questions.risk: recovery in Notion has time limits and depends on who has access. Miss the window, or lose the only person with edit rights, and the page is gone. Pages in a removed member's private section are hidden from everyone.

fixes.text: Know your windows: Trash keeps deleted pages 30 days by default. After they're deleted from Trash, they're kept another 30 days, then become inaccessible to everyone, even workspace owners.
Know your plan's version history: Free 7 days, Plus 30 days, Business 90 days, Enterprise unlimited.
Know who can restore: viewing and restoring version history needs at least Can edit access. Give at least 2 people Full access on every key page or teamspace.
Remove single points of failure: move key pages out of anyone's Private section into a teamspace. A removed member's private pages are hidden.
Last resort: Notion support can restore a snapshot of content from the past 30 days. Contact them through ? in the sidebar or team@makenotion.com.

plan_notes.text: Version history: Free 7 days, Plus 30 days, Business 90 days, Enterprise unlimited.
Enterprise only: custom Trash and retention settings. Free, Plus and Business alternative: act within the default 30-day Trash window, and name a recovery owner.

questions.title: Recovery and Traceability
questions.question: If an important page were deleted or overwritten today, could you get it back and see who did it?

A.text: Yes. We know how far back our plan goes and we've tested a restore.

B.text: Probably, through Trash or version history, but we've never tried.

C.text: I wouldn't know where to start.

questions.risk: a backup or history you've never tested is a hope, not a control. Most teams find their plan's limits on the day they need them.

fixes.text: Deleted pages: Trash at the bottom of the sidebar keeps them 30 days by default.
Overwritten pages: ••• → Version history → pick a version → Restore. It shows who made each change.
Run a 10-minute restore drill once a quarter on a test page.

plan_notes.text: Version history: Free 7 days, Plus 30 days, Business 90 days, Enterprise unlimited.
Enterprise only: audit log (up to 365 days of events, exportable to CSV). Free, Plus and Business alternative: version history and Trash (see Q11).

quick_wins.question: q3
quick_wins.title: See What's Public
quick_wins.text: Open any published page, select Share → Publish → All published sites, and Unpublish anything you don't recognize. Unpublishing doesn't remove "Anyone on the web with link" on a page, so check that in Share → General access too.
quick_wins.email: open any published page, select Share → Publish → All published sites, and unpublish anything you don't recognize.

quick_wins.question: q1
quick_wins.title: Turn On 2-Step Verification
quick_wins.text: Settings → your name → Account security → 2-step verification → Add verification method. Use an authenticator app, save the backup codes, and ask your team to do the same.
quick_wins.email: turn on 2-step verification: Settings → your name → Account security → 2-step verification → Add verification method.

quick_wins.title: Lock Key Pages
